primary.caveat: The calibration skill was written by an author who saw the entire suite, so no split is clean with respect to the author. This is a POSITIVE CONTROL on the instrument - does the detector fire when a real effect exists - not a claim that the skill generalizes.

caveats: Token counts are local estimates unless calibrated; see src/agent/tokens.py.

Public coding benchmarks are contamination-inflated by roughly 5-15 points, and an audit found ~59% of the hardest SWE-bench Verified tasks have tests that would not catch the intended bug. A reported 90% is realistically 75-80%.
Identical GAIA problems score anywhere from ~45% to ~92% depending only on the scaffold around the model.
Published agent costs have been misestimated by up to 100%. These numbers are cost-controlled but single-run unless n is stated.

secondary.caveat: Contamination-clean with respect to the drafting split, but UNDERPOWERED at this n. Report alongside the primary, never instead of it.
